liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Help On The Way** (1 review): Reviewer highlights the second set sequence starting with Help On The Way [27]

## The recordings

- **gd1984-04-21.u87.eaton-silberman.10035.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): source not stated; 23 songs; 180 min; rated 4.6/5 by 10 [1]
- **gd1984-04-21.148829.fob.schoeps.cmc4.mk41.bryant.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 24 songs; 170 min [8]
- **gd1984-04-21.neumannu87.bandrofcheck.34682.sbeok.shnf**: source not stated; 22 songs; 184 min; rated 2/5 by 1 [14]. Said about its sound: Recording is well EQ balanced and not overly cloudy despite an off night [34]
- **gd1984-04-21.166581.mtx.seamons.ht166.flac16**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 22 songs; 170 min [16]. Said about its sound: Lamarre's recording adds deep, resonant bass needed for these specific SBD mixes [16]

## Around the show

- Listener from Philadelphia suburbs surprised no one locally discussed the three-night Civic Center run [26]
- Reviewer attended at age 16, their first show, at the now-demolished Civic Center [27]
- Listener was nearly 20 and familiar with only half the material played [29]
- Bought a ticket for 30 dollars from an ad in The Philadelphia Journal [30]
- Audience member shouts Franklin's Tower name immediately after Slipknot ends [33]
- Shared beer, grilled cheese, and paper with a kid camping in a service room [35]
- Taper was very sick, started second set on wrong tape side, needed a third tape [14]
- Civic Center felt more intimate than the Spectrum, where the band usually played [28]
- Second set described as lackluster compared to the steady first set [34]
- Playing was raw and exploratory, with Brent and Jerry going in different directions [36]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1984-04-21.u87.eaton-silberman.10035.sbeok.shnf**: taped by Rob Eaton and Jeff Silberman; transferred by Doug Oade; source: Rob's Neumann u87 (cardiod setting, split 30', 17th row) > 6 x 9 volts > Teac mic transformers -> Jeff's Technics SV-100 line in @ 14 bits > DAT [1]. Also: Analog tape lineage: master cassette to DAT to cassette, acquired 15-20 years ago [33]
- **gd1984-04-21.148829.fob.schoeps.cmc4.mk41.bryant.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Robert Bryant; transferred by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller; source: Robert Bryant's Master (FOB) Audience Cassettes; Schoeps CMC4 MK41 mics > Sony D5 [8]. Also: FOB cassette source patched with Neumann U87 audio for China Doll and Drums transitions [8]
- **gd1984-04-21.neumannu87.bandrofcheck.34682.sbeok.shnf**: source: unknown shotgun mics > Sony D6 > Maxell MX 90s (MC) > Marantz PRD505 (azimuth adjusted) > Marantz Intergrated Stereo Amp MP-68 > SBLive! > SoundForge 5.0… [14]. Also: Neumann U87s into Sony Pro Mixer, Technics SV100 PCM, DAT, then CDR [14]
- **gd1984-04-21.166581.mtx.seamons.ht166.flac16**: source: Matrix by Hunter Seamons using Final Cut Pro (FLAC > AIFF > Final Cut w/EQ > AIFF CD tracking via Audacity > FLAC16 via xACT w/meta-tagging) December 26, 2023 [16]. Also: Matrix patches Neumann U87 DAT sections; SBD mixes had extended high end EQ'd [16]
